newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate falls on peso, U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate falls on peso, U.S. long bond.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates dropped 205 basis points to close at 19.35 percent on Thursday as recent pressure eased due to a stable peso and a sharp fall in U.S. long bond yields, traders and analysts said.
"Several factors came together, including the exchange rate and the U.S. bond market. The market had begun to feel stabler yesterday," one trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 0.1 of a centavo firmer at 7.9620/7.9650 per dollar.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 26/32 to yield 6.78 percent in late dealing.

A fixed-income analyst said rates had also subsided due to less speculative pressure arising from banks needing to settle outstanding balances on checking accounts with the central bank. The central bank's deadline for such settlements fell on Wednesday.
"The market has been less speculative, as yesterday was the central bank cutoff date," he said.
The analyst added that rates also fell because Banco de Mexico drained the relatively small amount of 417 million pesos from the market, through two repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile fell 150 basis points to 20.40 percent.

Liquidity of 942 million pesos was scheduled to return to the market on Friday from prior central bank participation. Dealers said they expected a liquidity shortfall, however, due to demand for cash prior to the weekend totalling 1.200 billion pesos.
